html:
Chagai-I was the code name of Pakistan's first nuclear tests, set off on 28 May 1998 inside the Ras Koh hills in the Chagai district of Balochistan, in reply to India's tests two weeks before.

Pakistan's programme began under Zulfikar Ali Bhutto after the loss of East Pakistan in 1971. The metallurgist A. Q. Khan, who had worked in the Netherlands, brought designs for uranium centrifuges. Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif ordered the tests in spite of US pressure, and a second test followed on 30 May.

Pakistan became the seventh country to declare nuclear weapons. Both countries faced sanctions. The tests are celebrated in Pakistan each 28 May. A year later the two fought the Kargil War, the first clash between nuclear states, and in 2004 A. Q. Khan admitted selling nuclear secrets to Iran, Libya and North Korea.
